title: Credit Policy Memorandum: Consumer Relationship Exposure Limit for the Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract
content:
Kestrel limits the total consumer credit it extends to one customer across products, and a Kestrel New Vehicle Retail Installment Sale Contract is funded only within that limit.

**Rule.** Relationship exposure is the sum of the principal balance on every open retail, pre-owned and balloon contract of the customer, plus the adjusted lease balance on every lease of the customer in active or maturity-extended status, plus the amount financed of the contract being booked. Relationship exposure must not exceed the relationship exposure cap of the tier being booked. When it would, the contract is not funded; there is no partial approval and no override at the servicing desk. Business customers' fleet units are commercial credit and never count toward consumer relationship exposure.

**Evidence.** The test is made on the company's records before the booking or funding: the customer's own Kestrel new-vehicle retail, pre-owned and balloon contracts and their principal balances, the customer's leases with their status and adjusted lease balance, and the amount financed of the contract being booked — all tied to the same customer. A customer's statement of what they owe elsewhere at Kestrel does not replace those records.

## What enters the sum

| Holding of the same customer | Included as |
|---|---|
| Open new-vehicle retail, pre-owned or balloon contract | its principal balance |
| Lease in active or maturity-extended status | its adjusted lease balance |
| Lease in any other status | nothing |
| Fleet unit under a business customer's fleet lease | nothing |
| The contract being booked | its amount financed |

## Hypothetical worked example

A customer applies for a Tier 2 contract with an amount financed of 30,000.00 dollars, holds an open pre-owned contract with a principal balance of 12,000.00 dollars and an active lease with an adjusted lease balance of 20,000.00 dollars. Relationship exposure is 12,000.00 plus 20,000.00 plus 30,000.00, a total of 62,000.00 dollars. The test compares that total with the Tier 2 relationship exposure cap: the contract is funded only if the total does not exceed it; a total equal to the cap does not exceed it.
